neighbours.label: The slot right before 'induced' in experimental biomedicine: the adverb or modifier of a condition that was deliberately produced (experimentally / chemically / drug- induced), vs the same adverbs before other verbs
fire: In the study, seizures were experimentally induced in young mice.
Colitis was chemically induced in the rats by adding a compound to their water.
The researchers examined stress-induced changes in heart rate.
Hypertension was surgically induced in the dogs before the drug trial.
Patients with noise-induced hearing loss were recruited for the trial.
Diabetes was experimentally induced in the animals with a single injection.
The team measured exercise-induced asthma in teenage athletes.
Inflammation was chemically induced in the paw of each mouse.
quiet: In the study, the findings were experimentally confirmed in young mice.
The water was chemically analyzed in the lab before the rats drank it.
The researchers examined daily changes in heart rate.
The tumor was surgically removed from the dogs before the drug trial.
Patients with mild hearing loss were recruited for the trial.
The animals were experimentally tested with a single injection of saline.
The team measured lung capacity in teenage athletes.
Swelling was carefully measured in the paw of each mouse.

predictions: Fire 0.2-0.5 on the adverb or hyphen before 'induced'; near misses with the same adverb before confirmed/measured under 0.1.
notes: Card: experiment-ally, -ind, drug-, 'used to', 'mood' (elicitation) before induction words; logit effect promotes ' induced'. Probe: 'Arrhythmias were experimentally induced' 0.521, 'mood elicitation' 0.202, 'drug- and alcohol-induced' 0.158, 'used to induce' 0.078; 'results were experimentally confirmed' 0.024, 'treated with antibiotics' 0.017.
